dog.basis: Smaller dogs generally use lower medication and anesthesia doses; CareCredit notes that pet size affects veterinary costs.
Medium is the neutral forecast baseline.
Larger dogs generally use higher medication and anesthesia doses; Pawlicy Advisor notes that larger breeds typically cost more to care for.
First-year care commonly includes several vaccine visits and sterilization; Pawlicy Advisor estimates $1,000-$2,000 for first-year routine care.
Adult dogs age 1-6 are the neutral forecast baseline.
Older pets are more likely to need added lab work and more frequent monitoring; Pawlicy Advisor notes that older pets typically cost more to care for.

cat.basis: First-year care commonly includes several vaccine visits and sterilization; Pawlicy Advisor estimates $1,000-$2,000 for first-year routine care.
Adult cats age 1-6 are the neutral forecast baseline.
Older cats commonly receive added bloodwork and urinalysis during wellness care; PetMD describes expanded screening for senior pets.
